name: Razorpay/UPI Payment Reconciliation - Settlement & Bank Matching with Failed-Payment Recovery

parameters.content:
# Razorpay / UPI Payment Reconciliation with Settlement Matching and Failed-Payment Recovery

Razorpay tells you a payment was captured, a different report tells you when it was settled, and your bank statement tells you when the money actually arrived. Finance teams stitch these together by hand, and failed UPI payments quietly become unpaid invoices. This workflow does the full chain every morning: **invoice -> payment -> settlement -> bank credit**, and recovers failed payments with a fresh payment link.

## How it works
1. **Load state.** Reads Invoices, Bank Credits, the Payments Ledger and open Exceptions from Google Sheets.
2. **Fetch from Razorpay.** Pulls payments for the lookback window, the settlement recon report per day and the settlements list, all with pagination.
3. **Match.** Each payment is matched to an invoice by manual override, invoice reference in notes or order receipt, then Razorpay order ID. Unreferenced payments with a strong customer + amount match become Probable Matches; the rest go to GPT for a suggested invoice, which is only ever a suggestion.
4. **Reconcile.** Handles partial, over and duplicate payments and refunds. Rolls payments into settlements, confirms each settlement UTR against your bank credits, checks fees against your plan, and flags delayed settlements, holds and uncaptured authorizations.
5. **Recover failed payments.** Failures are categorised (cancelled, insufficient funds, UPI limit, wrong PIN/VPA, timeout, bank down). After a retry grace period, a new Razorpay payment link is created, the old one is cancelled, and GPT writes a reminder matched to the failure reason. Up to 3 attempts, then escalation.
6. **Report.** Receipts go to customers who just paid. Finance gets an HTML report and Slack gets a digest with success rate by method and high-severity exceptions.

## Setup steps
1. Create a Google Sheet with tabs **Invoices, Payments Ledger, Settlements, Exceptions, Bank Credits** (headers in the section notes) and paste the ID into every Sheets node.
2. Create an **HTTP Basic Auth** credential with your Razorpay Key ID as user and Key Secret as password, and select it in the four Razorpay nodes. Start with test keys.
3. Connect Google Sheets, Gmail, OpenAI and Slack.
4. Fill in company details, emails and your fee rates in **Set Recon Rules**.
5. When you create orders or links elsewhere, put the invoice ID in the order receipt or in notes.invoice_id so matching is exact.

## 1. Schedule & rules
Runs at 7:30 AM daily. **Set Recon Rules** holds lookback windows, tolerances, settlement and bank SLAs, retry grace period, chase limits, link expiry and expected fee % per method (JSON). Settlements usually arrive T+2 working days, so reconDays of 5 catches them.

## 2. Load state from Sheets
**Invoices:** Invoice ID, Customer Name, Customer Email, Customer Phone, Amount, Currency, Due Date, Status, Razorpay Order ID, Paid Amount, Balance Due, Payment IDs, Payment Method, Paid On, Settlement ID, UTR, Settled On, Fee, GST on Fee, Net Received, Recon Status, Last Recon Run, Payment Link ID, Payment Link URL, Link Expires, Chase Count, Last Chase Date, Last Chase Stage, Last Failure Reason
**Bank Credits:** Date, Amount, UTR, Reference, Narration (paste or export from your bank)
Reference tabs are read once per run and tolerate being empty.

## 3. Fetch from Razorpay
Payments (`/v1/payments`), settlement recon per day (`/v1/settlements/recon/combined`) and settlements (`/v1/settlements`). Each call pages with `skip` until a short page, with retries and a small delay between requests.

## 4. Reconciliation engine
One Code node produces every record type: invoice updates, ledger rows, settlements, exceptions, receipts, link cancellations, chases and the summary. Resolved or Ignored exceptions in the sheet are never re-raised. The router sends each type to its branch; the AI branch runs first so the report can include its suggestions.

## 5. AI match suggestions
Payments with no invoice reference but some candidate invoices are sent to GPT with up to 15 candidates. The pick is validated against the candidate list and written to Exceptions. It is never applied automatically: confirm by typing the ID into **Manual Invoice ID** on the Payments Ledger.

## 6. Ledgers & exceptions
**Payments Ledger:** Payment ID, Created At, Status, Method, Amount, Refunded, Fee, GST on Fee, Customer Email, Customer Contact, VPA, Invoice ID, Match Method, Order ID, Settlement ID, UTR, Settled At, Error Code, Error Reason, Failure Category, Recon Note, Updated On, Manual Invoice ID
**Settlements:** Settlement ID, Created On, Amount, Fees, GST on Fees, UTR, Razorpay Status, Payments, Bank Status, Bank Date, Updated On
**Exceptions:** Exception Key, Type, Severity, Entity ID, Invoice ID, Customer, Amount, Detail, Suggested Action, First Detected, Last Seen, Status (set Resolved or Ignored to silence)

## 7. Receipts, links & failed-payment recovery
Newly paid invoices get a receipt. Links for paid or replaced invoices are cancelled so nobody pays twice. For failures, a fresh link is created and GPT writes a reminder specific to the failure reason and attempt number. Attempt 3 or high-value balances alert Slack. A failed send does not count as an attempt.

## 8. Daily report
HTML report to finance and a Slack digest: captured, fees, settled, bank-confirmed, success rate by method, failure mix, and exceptions ranked by severity.

## Credentials & security
Razorpay keys live in an n8n HTTP Basic Auth credential, never in the workflow. Google, Gmail and Slack use OAuth2, OpenAI an API key. Only unmatched-payment details and failure reasons are sent to OpenAI, never card or bank data. Keep the sheet restricted: it holds customer contacts and payment data.

values.content: You help an Indian finance team match a Razorpay payment that has no invoice reference to one of their open invoices. Use the payer email, phone, UPI VPA (the handle often contains the payer's name or business), description, notes and amount. Only pick an invoice from the candidate list. Amount equal to the balance is strong evidence; a different customer with the same amount is weak evidence. If nothing is convincing, return null. Return only JSON: {"invoiceId": "..." or null, "confidence": 0-1, "reason": "one short sentence"}

values.content: You write short payment-recovery emails for an Indian business whose customer's online payment failed. Be warm and practical, never blame the customer. Tailor the advice to the failure category: cancelled = maybe they closed the app by mistake, here is a fresh link; insufficient_funds = gentle, suggest another account or card, no mention of balance amounts; limit_exceeded = UPI daily or per-transaction limit, suggest net banking, card, or paying from another UPI app or account; details_incorrect = check UPI PIN, OTP or UPI ID; timeout = the approval request expired, approve within a few minutes next time; bank_issue = the bank had a temporary problem, not their fault, please retry; other = something went wrong, please retry. Attempt 1 is a friendly heads-up, attempt 2 a polite follow-up, attempt 3 mentions this is the last automated reminder and that someone from the team will call. Always include the payment link on its own line and the support contact. Under 120 words, plain text, no bracketed placeholders, sign off as 'Accounts Team' followed by the company name. Return only JSON: {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}
